facts.text: Dispatch order inside `dispatch_qmv` (mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp, main): (1) K == 64 or K == 128 with power-of-2 bits and no global scale goes to `qmv_quad`, before qmv_wide is considered; (2) else M >= 2 and `use_qmv_wide(mode, d)` and no global scale goes to `qmv_wide`; (3) else plain `qmv`. `use_qmv_wide` is `mode != "affine" || arch_gen >= 15`.
nvfp4 with a tensor-level global scale never takes qmv_wide (falls to `qmv`). The same function is also reached from the qqmm path (activation-quantized matmul), so those shapes follow the same rule.
Only transposed-weight matmuls reach it; the non-transposed case uses `vector_limit = 4` and the qvm path.
Upper bound is `vector_limit = get_qmv_batch_limit(K, N, d)`; at or above it, qmm (or `qmm_splitk` when B == 1) runs instead. This limit is per generation and per chip tier, not a single 13:
gen >= 17 non-Ultra (M5 Pro/Max class): 33 if K,N <= 2048; 25 if both <= 4096; else 13.
gen 15-16 non-Ultra (M3/M4 Pro/Max class): 13; 15; 13 by the same size bands.
So the 12-to-13 crossover cited elsewhere holds for M3/M4/M5 Pro and Max on large matrices, not for Ultra (12) or M1/M2 base-Pro-Max (6 on large matrices).

Tiling (qmv_wide host function): `n_tiles = ceil(M/5)`, `vecs_per_tg = ceil(M/n_tiles)`. Each tile re-reads the weights, so weight streams per matmul = ceil(M/5). M=2..5: 1 stream; M=6..10: 2 streams (3-5 rows each); M=11..13: 3 streams. Grid is (n_tiles, ceil(N/rows_per_tg), B) with 2 simdgroups per threadgroup.

k_lanes (lanes reducing K per output row): 8 for affine (4 output rows per simdgroup, 8 per threadgroup), 16 for fp modes (2 rows per simdgroup, 4 per threadgroup). Reduction uses a simd_shuffle_down ladder, not simd_sum.

Affine decode: each lane strides over groups, decodes the group in 8-value sub-chunks (`scale*q+bias`, accumulate in fp32), and reuses each sub-chunk across vecs_per_tg vectors. `group_size/8` is unrolled, so any group size that is a multiple of 8 works; kernel name encodes `_gs_`, `_b_`, `_nv_`, `_kl_`, `_batch_`.
Scale/bias are loaded once per group per lane, so metadata traffic per weight byte depends on group size exactly as in qmv; there is no group-size special case in the dispatch.
Reviewer fix (angeloskath, 26 Jun 2026): in the fp kernel, the per-group scale multiply was applied to nf4*4 = 32 values; moving it after the dot product cut it to one multiply.
PR 3764 opened 24 Jun 2026, approved 26 Jun, merged 26 Jun as 548dd80; v0.32.0 was released 7 Jul 2026. v0.32.1 (17 Aug), v0.32.2 (25 Aug), v0.32.3 (28 Sep, latest) followed.

PR 3888 `gemv_wide` (jessegross, merged 22 Jul 2026, in 0.32.1): the bf16/fp16 sibling of qmv_wide for the layers a quantized model leaves unquantized, x @ w.T with M = 2..15, streams weight rows once for up to 5 vectors, covers Matmul, AddMM, GatherMM, M3 generation and later. Per-kernel speedups: `in_proj_a/b` [M,2048]x[2048,32] M=2: 3.0x M3 Ultra, 2.3x M4 Pro, 6.0x M5 Max; M=8: 2.3x, 1.7x, 4.8x. `lm_head` [M,2048]x[2048,248320] M=2: 1.7x, 2.3x, 1.4x; M=8: 1.8x, 2.1x, 1.3x.

v0.32.1 also fixed nvfp4 `quantized_matmul` through the split-K path (PR 3854). v0.32.3 added Metal global-scale qmm (PR 4458, 4483) and fixed fp quantized matmul corruption when the quantized dim is not a multiple of 32 (PR 3912).
Split-K qmm for small M (PR 3120) landed before 0.32.0; qmm_splitk picks split_k to target about 512 threadgroups and requires K partitions that are whole multiples of max(group_size, 32).

M1 is generation 13 and M2 is generation 14 (M3 Pro reports `applegpu_g15s`); affine quantization on M1/M2 stays on `qmv` at all M. fp-format quants (nvfp4, mxfp4, mxfp8) still get qmv_wide there: the PR table measures M2 Pro at 1.3x (M=2) and 1.4-1.7x (M=4, 8), so "M1/M2 get nothing" is true only for int4/int8 affine.

The PR benchmark has only one shape (Gemma-4-12B gate/up 15360x3840, bf16 activations, GPU kernel time) and four chips (M2 Pro, M3 Ultra, M4 Pro, M5 Max); no M1, no M3 base/Pro/Max, no M4 Max, no group size other than the default.
At M=2, affine int4 gain is only 1.1-1.3x and int8 on M4 Pro is 1.0x; mxfp4 is the weakest fp mode at M=8 (1.2-1.4x) while mxfp8 and nvfp4 reach 1.7-2.2x.
Kernel-time speedups are not end-to-end: an M5 Max reviewer figure is mxfp4 Qwen 9B batch 4 going 253 to 295 tok/s (after the scale hoist), +17%.
Shapes with K of 64 or 128 skip qmv_wide for qmv_quad; shapes with a tensor global scale skip it.
Backports to older mlx pins must carry the `use_qmv_wide` gate: spokvulcan/mlx 452aeca (21 Aug 2026) ported only the affine half onto v0.31.1 and relies on the gen>=15 check.

Existing dossier says mlx 0.32.0 widened the verify window; issue 4265's author measured no change between 0.31.2 and 0.32.0 on M3 Ultra. Source explains part of it: Ultra uses the 'd' branch (vector_limit 12 on large matrices), M3 Ultra is gen 15 so affine qualifies, so the kernel was reachable there; the discrepancy is not a gating miss.
No published end-to-end draft-width sweep keyed to ceil(M/5) steps (M=5 vs M=6 should show a step in verify cost on large matrices); not measured in any source read.
No measured effect of group size (g32/g64/g128) on qmv_wide speedup.
No M1 or M3 base measurements; no data on whether extending the affine gate to gen 13-14 is ever profitable.
Whether the tile cap of 5 will be raised or the kernel replaced by a split-K/MMA variant (issue 4265 invited a PR; none merged in sources read).
`dispatch_qmv` routes K==64 or K==128 (power-of-2 bits, no global scale) to `qmv_quad` before considering qmv_wide.
qmv_wide is used when M >= 2, `use_qmv_wide(mode, d)` holds, and no global scale is present.
`use_qmv_wide` returns `mode != "affine" || arch_gen >= 15`.
nvfp4 with a tensor global scale falls back to plain `qmv`.
qmv_wide uses `n_tiles = ceil(M/5)` and `vecs_per_tg = ceil(M/n_tiles)`, so weights are read ceil(M/5) times.
qmv_wide runs 2 simdgroups per threadgroup with k_lanes 8 for affine and 16 for fp modes.
The affine qmv_wide decodes each group in 8-value sub-chunks with fp32 accumulation and unrolls group_size/8 chunks.
`get_qmv_batch_limit` on gen>=17 non-Ultra returns 33, 25, 13 for K,N <=2048, <=4096, larger.
`get_qmv_batch_limit` on gen 15-16 non-Ultra returns 13, 15, 13 by the same size bands.
`get_qmv_batch_limit` for gen>=13 Ultra ('d') returns 32, 18, 12 and for gen 13-14 non-Ultra returns 14, 10, 6.
When M >= vector_limit and B == 1 with transposed weights, MLX uses `qmm_splitk`, which targets about 512 threadgroups.
PR 3764 was merged 26 Jun 2026 and v0.32.0 was released 7 Jul 2026 with it in the notes.
On M2 Pro, fp-mode qmv_wide measured 1.3x at M=2 and 1.4-1.7x at M=4 and M=8, while int4 and int8 stayed on qmv.
PR 3764 benchmarks cover M2 Pro, M3 Ultra, M4 Pro and M5 Max on one shape (15360x3840, bf16 activations) only.
PR 3888 (gemv_wide) merged 22 Jul 2026 and shipped in v0.32.1.
gemv_wide handles bf16/fp16 x @ w.T with M = 2..15 on M3-generation and later GPUs for Matmul, AddMM and GatherMM.
gemv_wide measured 2.3-6.0x on `in_proj_a/b` M=2 across M3 Ultra, M4 Pro, M5 Max and 1.3-2.3x on a 248320-wide lm_head.
v0.32.1 fixed nvfp4 quantized_matmul via split-K (PR 3854); v0.32.3 added Metal global-scale qmm (PR 4458, 4483) and an fp quantized matmul corruption fix for dims not multiple of 32 (PR 3912).
mlx v0.32.3 (28 Sep 2026) is the latest release as of this fetch.
M3 Pro reports Metal architecture `applegpu_g15s`.
M1 is generation 13 and M2 is generation 14 in MLX's architecture-gen numbering.
To check you have qmv_wide: `mx.__version__ >= 0.32.0` and `mx.metal.device_info()["architecture"]` ends in a gen >= 15 for affine; fp modes need only the version.
Verify cost for a batch of M rows steps up at M=6 and M=11 on qmv_wide because weight streams go 1 to 2 to 3; draft width 4 plus the bonus row (M=5) is the last single-stream width.
Group size has no dispatch effect on qmv_wide; only per-group metadata traffic differs.
